question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Fracture of ulnar shaft with dislocation of radial head -> surgical treatment -> possible nerve injury -> 70% CHAIN: Weakness in extending middle finger -> radial deviation on wrist extension -> possible radial nerve involvement -> 60% CHAIN: Pain and weakness in right forearm and hand -> tenderness distal to lateral epicondyle -> possible radial nerve compression -> 50% CHAIN: Marked weakness in extending middle finger -> possible extensor muscle dysfunction -> possible radial nerve injury -> 40% CHAIN: Sensation not impaired -> rules out sensory nerve involvement -> less likely ulnar nerve -> 70%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of weakness in extending the middle finger and radial deviation on wrist extension suggest a radial nerve injury. The location of tenderness and the history of previous ulnar shaft fracture with radial head dislocation also point towards radial nerve involvement.
